+# Shackle a trailer's towing lug and lock the pin with one twist
+
+A small two-wheeled utility trailer stands on the table, its drawbar ending in a steel block with a towing lug toward
+the robot. A 1/2 in D shackle stands upright in a slotted stand left of the trailer; its red quick-lock pin stands in
+a holder on the right. The robot must hang the shackle's two ears around the lug, push the pin through the upper ear,
+the lug's hole and into the lower ear, and lock it with one twist.
+
+**Instruction:** `Shackle the trailer's towing lug: the lug between the shackle's ears and the pin screwed home to lock it.`
+
+## Why this task
+
+Coupling a trailer, cart or skip to whatever will tow or lift it is routine work for industrial truck and tractor
+operators (O*NET 53-7051, about 800,000 US workers) and riggers (O*NET 49-9096). The shackle is a loose part: two ears
+20.6 mm apart must straddle a 15 mm lug and stay square while a 15.8 mm pin goes through three holes in a row with
+under 1 mm of play each. One hand has to hold the shackle in place while the other brings the pin, then the pin must
+be locked: an unlocked pin can work out under load. It is not a plain peg-in-hole: the hole the pin goes into is
+formed only while the shackle is held in place around the lug, and it moves if the shackle is let go too early or
+knocked.
+
+## Design
+
+| Object | Size | Mass | Notes |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Trailer | Deck 42 x 34 cm, 2 cm thick, underside 10 cm up, 5 cm rails on both sides and the back; one axle, two 18 cm wheels 4 cm wide | fixed | Blue painted steel deck, rubber wheels. From x 40 to 82 cm, centred at y -8 cm |
+| Drawbar block | 8 x 8 cm, 7.75 cm tall, x 32 to 40, y -12 to -4 cm | fixed | Painted steel; a riser joins it to the deck |
+| Towing lug | 15 mm steel plate, 40 mm wide, projecting 5 cm toward the arms, top flush with the block's top (centre 7 cm up); 19 mm square hole centred at x 29, y -8 cm | fixed | Part of the block |
+| Shackle | 1/2 in D shackle: 12.7 mm bar, round ears 27 mm across and 12.7 mm thick, 20.6 mm apart, 47.8 mm inside length | 0.25 kg | Galvanised steel. Upper ear: plain 17.5 mm hole. Lower ear: the pin's thread under a 3.5 mm plain lead-in. Stands upright, threaded ear down, bow toward the arms, at x 27, y 7 cm in a slotted pine stand (10 mm base) |
+| Pin | 15.8 mm x 46 mm under a 25 mm collar; flat eye 26 x 8 mm on top; 1.5 mm x 45 degree chamfer at its end | 0.11 kg | Steel, red. Quick-lock thread (see below). Stands eye up in a hole through a pine block 4 x 4 x 3 cm at x 22, y -23 cm |
+
+- **Quick-lock pin:** the pin's thread has a steep lead, so half a turn takes it from the thread's first catch to the
+  collar seated on the upper ear (9.2 mm of travel). Turned 120 degrees clockwise, it is locked.
+- **Why the shackle starts upright:** the gripper's fingers (26 mm wide) do not fit inside the shackle's 20.6 mm
+  opening, and turning a flat shackle upright would need a horizontal grip the left arm cannot reach. The stand
+  holds it the way it hangs on a rigging rack.
+- **Why the lug is 7 cm up:** holding the pin straight down above a higher lug is out of the right arm's reach.
+
+## Scoring
+
+Evaluated every control step; the score at the end of the episode counts (`SCORE_OVER = "end"`).
+
+| Condition | Score |
+|---|---|
+| The shackle or the pin at any point fell off the table, or the pin is not through the upper ear, the lug and into the lower ear | 0 |
+| Pin through all three and locked: turned at least 120 degrees clockwise on its thread, or its collar within 1 mm of the upper ear (success, held 1 s) | 1.0 |
+| Pin through all three, thread caught, turned at least 45 degrees | 0.5 |
+| Pin through all three, not turned | 0.25 |
+
+- "Through" means the pin's axis passes through the lug's hole at the lug's mid-plane, tilted under 15 degrees, its
+  end below the lug and its collar above it; and it lies on the shackle's axis within 3 mm, tilted under 10 degrees,
+  its end into the lower ear.
+- In a real trial: a line on the eye and a matching mark on the upper ear show the turn (120 degrees is a third of a
+  turn); a look at the pin shows whether it passes through all three; the video shows anything falling off.
+
+Unintended strategies and what stops them:
+- Putting the pin through the shackle without the lug between the ears: no credit (the pin must pass through the
+  lug's hole).
+- Pushing the pin through the lug alone, or lying the parts on the trailer: no credit.
+- Turning the pin before it is through all three: the thread only catches with the pin's end resting centred on the
+  lower ear.
+- Throwing or dropping the parts off the table: 0.
+
+## Scripted demo
+
+```bash
+inspect-robots run --embodiment yam_arena --policy yam_scripted \
+  -E task=task.py -E object_jitter=0 -E control_hz=20 -E cam_width=320 -E cam_height=176 \
+  --instruction "Shackle the trailer's towing lug: the lug between the shackle's ears and the pin screwed home to lock it." \
+  --scorer task_score \
+  --max-steps 1200 --store-frames --log-dir ~/yam-eval/trailer-towing-shackle-demo
+```
+
+1. **Left arm** grips the shackle's bow, leaning 35 degrees forward, lifts it out of its stand, carries it in front of
+   the lug, lines the ears up with the lug and slides them over it, and holds it there.
+2. **Right arm** lifts the pin out of its holder by the eye, brings it over the lug and lowers it through the upper ear
+   and the lug onto the lower ear, where the thread catches. It lets go and rises.
+3. **Left arm** lets go of the shackle and moves away.
+4. **Right arm** grips the eye again and gives it one clockwise twist (half a turn plus 35 degrees, the wrist's limit;
+   the fingers slip a little on the eye). The pin locks.
+
+`yam_scripted` plays fixed waypoints, so the demo is open loop. It uses offsets measured in simulation for each arm's
+sag under load and for the shackle's 2.35 degree tilt in the left grip.
+
+`SHACKLE_DEBUG=1` prints the shackle's and pin's poses, the thread's state and the turn every 0.2 s. It is off by
+default.
+
+## Files
+
+| File | What |
+|---|---|
+| `task.py` | The yam_arena task file: trailer, lug, shackle, pin and stands, the thread emulation, `score()` / `success()`, and `demo()` |
+| `jointkit.py` | Rigid parts made of boxes, joints between parts that can be switched on and off and driven at run time, and per-physics-step and reset hooks (hooks yam_arena without modifying it) |
+| `test_trailer_towing_shackle.py` | The task file loads, the lock geometry, one twist in the demo, the demo's reach |
+| `task.json` | Submission details |
+
+## Runtime and seeds
+
+A demo run (Isaac Sim start, reset, 550 control steps) takes about 4 minutes of wall time on an RTX workstation. Run
+limit: 1,200 steps (1 minute at 20 Hz). The layout is fixed, so always pass `-E object_jitter=0`. There is no other
+randomness.
+
+## Tests
+
+```bash
+python -m pytest -q      # in this folder, in the yam_arena environment; no GPU needed
+```
+
+## Verified in simulation
+
+Isaac Lab-Arena (Isaac Lab 3.0, Isaac Sim 6.1), with the command above.
+
+| Run | `task_score` | What the log and video show |
+|---|---|---|
+| Scripted demo | **1.0** | The shackle goes on the lug, the pin drops through onto the lower ear and the thread catches; one twist locks it. Success at step 550 (27.5 s) |
+| Dream-1 | **0** | 1,200 steps (step limit). Both arms draw back toward their bases within the first seconds and stay there; neither touches the shackle or the pin, and nothing on the table moves |
+| `python -m pytest -q` | 6 passed | |
+
+## Real-world build
+
+- **Trailer:** any small two-wheeled utility or garden trailer, or a mock-up of its drawbar, braked or chocked so it
+  cannot roll. The lug is a 15 mm steel plate welded to the drawbar's end with a 19 mm hole.
+- **Shackle:** a standard 1/2 in screw-pin D shackle. The pin is a quick-lock variant (steep thread: half a turn seats
+  it); a standard 5/8-11 screw pin needs four turns instead.
+- **Stand and holder:** a pine stand with a slot that holds the shackle upright by its lower ear, and a pine block with
+  a 17 mm hole for the pin.
+- **Safety:** the parts are light and blunt; nothing is under load during the trial.
+
+## Still approximate or unverified
+
+- The thread is emulated (a joint that turns and slides, with friction), not modelled as a helix.
+- All parts are rigid; round parts are 16-sided prisms, and the wheels are drawn as stacked slabs.
+- The demo relies on offsets measured in simulation; with jitter it would miss.
+- One Dream-1 run (1,200 steps) scored 0: neither arm reached the shackle or the pin.

+"""jointkit: multi-box rigid parts, optionally with one spring-driven hinge, for a yam_arena task file.
+
+yam_arena task files only take single primitives (Box, Cylinder, Sphere, library assets). This module adds:
+
+- ``Part``: one loose rigid body made of several boxes (a hollow bottle, a cup, a cap with a hole in it). With a
+  ``Hinge`` it becomes a two-link articulation: the part and a child body on a revolute joint with a spring drive
+  (an implicit actuator), whose target the task file can change at run time (``set_hinge_target``).
+- ``PartState``: what ``success()/score()`` get for a Part: the body origin's pose (not a bounding-box centre), its
+  velocities, a world bounding box, and the hinge angle (rad).
+- ``on_step`` / ``on_reset``: callbacks run with the Isaac Lab env after every control step (before scoring) and
+  after every reset.
+- ``Attach``: a revolute joint from another Part to this one (outside any articulation), with a spring-damper drive
+  whose target (``set_attach_target``) and enabled state (``set_attached``) the task file can change at run time.
+- ``ball``: a sphere spawned with the same solver settings as the parts.
+- ``set_collision``: switch some of a Part's boxes' collision on or off at run time.
+- ``on_physics``: callbacks run before every physics step (240 Hz), for mechanisms that need more than 20 Hz.
+- An ``Attach`` with ``travel > 0`` is a screw-type joint (a D6): free turning about z plus sliding along z within
+  ``[0, travel]``, each with its own drive (``set_attach_target(..., height=)``).
+- ``Attach(enabled=False)`` spawns the joint switched off, for a part that is attached only later in the trial.
+
+Importing it hooks ``yam_arena.scene`` (spawning and state), ``yam_arena.inspect_embodiment`` (step and reset) and
+``yam_arena.demo`` (a ``Waypoint.yaw`` may be a 3x3 world rotation matrix, so ``yam_scripted`` can play grips other
+than straight down). yam_arena itself is not modified. Pure Python at import; Isaac Sim is imported lazily.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import importlib.abc
+import importlib.util
+import math
+import sys
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+
+import numpy as np
+from yam_arena.task_file import Box, ObjectState
+
+Color = tuple[float, float, float]
+# centre, size (m), sRGB colour (or RGBA: the 4th value is the opacity; 0 = a collider that is not drawn),
+# optionally a yaw about z (degrees) and then a pitch about the box's own y axis (degrees, applied before the yaw)
+BoxSpec = tuple
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Hinge:
+    """A child body on a revolute joint. ``anchor`` is the joint's point in the part frame and the child frame's
+    origin; ``boxes`` are in the child frame with the hinge closed (angle 0). The joint turns about the part's x axis
+    rotated ``yaw`` about z. A drive of ``stiffness`` (N m/rad) and ``damping`` (N m s/rad) pulls it to its target."""
+
+    name: str
+    anchor: tuple[float, float, float]
+    boxes: tuple[BoxSpec, ...]
+    lower: float = 0.0  # rad
+    upper: float = 2.0
+    yaw: float = 0.0
+    stiffness: float = 0.3
+    damping: float = 0.002
+    mass: float = 0.003
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Attach:
+    """A free-spinning revolute joint (about z of the joint frame) from another Part's body to this Part's body,
+    outside any articulation. ``pos0``/``rot0``: joint frame in the other part; ``pos1``/``rot1``: in this part.
+    An angular drive (``stiffness`` N m/rad toward a target angle that ``set_attach_target`` moves at run time, plus
+    ``damping`` N m s/rad) opposes turning and reacts on both bodies. ``set_attached`` switches the joint off (and on
+    again) at run time."""
+
+    to: str
+    pos0: tuple[float, float, float]
+    pos1: tuple[float, float, float] = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
+    rot0: float = 0.0  # yaw (rad) of the joint frame in the other part
+    rot1: float = 0.0
+    stiffness: float = 0.0
+    damping: float = 0.08
+    travel: float = 0.0  # > 0: also slides along z in [0, travel] (m), with the linear drive below
+    lin_stiffness: float = 0.0  # N/m
+    lin_damping: float = 0.0  # N s/m
+    lin_max_force: float = 1e6  # N
+    enabled: bool = True  # False: the joint starts switched off (set_attached turns it on)
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Part(Box):
+    """A loose rigid body made of ``boxes`` (part frame, origin at ``pos``). Subclasses Box so yam_arena's task-file
+    checks accept it; ``size`` is the boxes' extent and ``lo``/``hi`` its corners in the part frame."""
+
+    boxes: tuple[BoxSpec, ...] = ()
+    hinge: Hinge | None = None
+    attach: Attach | None = None
+    friction: float = 0.9
+    lo: tuple[float, float, float] = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
+    hi: tuple[float, float, float] = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
+    radius: float = 0.0  # > 0: one sphere collider instead of boxes
+    contact_offset: float = 0.001  # m; PhysX makes contacts within the sum of both shapes' offsets
+    ccd: bool = False  # speculative CCD, for a small part that can move fast against thin walls
+
+    def _check(self) -> None:
+        super()._check()
+        if not (self.boxes or self.radius > 0) or self.mass is None:
+            raise ValueError(f"{self.name}: a Part needs boxes (or a radius) and a mass")
+
+
+def part(name, pos, boxes, mass, yaw=0.0, hinge=None, color=(0.5, 0.5, 0.5), friction=0.9, attach=None,
+         contact_offset=0.001, ccd=False) -> Part:
+    lo = np.min([np.subtract(c, np.divide(s, 2)) for c, s, *_ in boxes], axis=0)
+    hi = np.max([np.add(c, np.divide(s, 2)) for c, s, *_ in boxes], axis=0)
+    return Part(name=name, pos=tuple(pos), size=tuple((hi - lo).tolist()), mass=mass, color=color, yaw=yaw,
+                boxes=tuple(boxes), hinge=hinge, attach=attach, friction=friction, lo=tuple(lo.tolist()),
+                hi=tuple(hi.tolist()), contact_offset=contact_offset, ccd=ccd)
+
+
+def ball(name, pos, radius, mass, color=(0.5, 0.5, 0.5), friction=0.3) -> Part:
+    """A sphere, spawned by this kit so that it gets the same solver settings (32 position iterations, 1 m/s
+    depenetration) as the parts it rolls around in."""
+    r = float(radius)
+    return Part(name=name, pos=tuple(pos), size=(2 * r,) * 3, mass=mass, color=color, friction=friction,
+                lo=(-r, -r, -r), hi=(r, r, r), radius=r)
+
+
+def quat_to_matrix(q) -> np.ndarray:
+    x, y, z, w = np.asarray(q, float) / np.linalg.norm(q)
+    return np.array([[1 - 2 * (y * y + z * z), 2 * (x * y - w * z), 2 * (x * z + w * y)],
+                     [2 * (x * y + w * z), 1 - 2 * (x * x + z * z), 2 * (y * z - w * x)],
+                     [2 * (x * z - w * y), 2 * (y * z + w * x), 1 - 2 * (x * x + y * y)]])
+
+
+def matrix_to_quat(r: np.ndarray) -> tuple[float, float, float, float]:
+    """XYZW, robust for any rotation (Shepperd)."""
+    t = np.trace(r)
+    if t > 0:
+        s = 2 * math.sqrt(t + 1)
+        return ((r[2, 1] - r[1, 2]) / s, (r[0, 2] - r[2, 0]) / s, (r[1, 0] - r[0, 1]) / s, s / 4)
+    i = int(np.argmax(np.diag(r)))
+    j, k = (i + 1) % 3, (i + 2) % 3
+    s = 2 * math.sqrt(1 + r[i, i] - r[j, j] - r[k, k])
+    q = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, (r[k, j] - r[j, k]) / s]
+    q[i], q[j], q[k] = s / 4, (r[j, i] + r[i, j]) / s, (r[k, i] + r[i, k]) / s
+    return tuple(q)
+
+
+def rot_z(a: float) -> np.ndarray:
+    c, s = math.cos(a), math.sin(a)
+    return np.array([[c, -s, 0.0], [s, c, 0.0], [0.0, 0.0, 1.0]])
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class PartState(ObjectState):
+    """A Part after a control step: body origin pose, velocities, world bounding box, hinge angle (rad)."""
+
+    hinge: float = 0.0
+    R: np.ndarray = field(default=None, repr=False)
+
+    def rotation(self) -> np.ndarray:
+        return quat_to_matrix(self.quat_xyzw) if self.R is None else self.R
+
+    def to_local(self, p) -> np.ndarray:
+        return self.rotation().T @ (np.asarray(p, float) - self.pos)
+
+    def to_world(self, p) -> np.ndarray:
+        return self.pos + self.rotation() @ np.asarray(p, float)
+
+    def tilt(self) -> float:
+        """Angle (rad) between the part's z axis and the vertical."""
+        return math.acos(max(-1.0, min(1.0, float(self.rotation()[2, 2]))))
+
+
+# -- spawning (Isaac Sim only) ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+_SPECS: dict[str, Part] = {}
+_JOINTS: dict[str, str] = {}  # part name -> its attach joint's prim path (the first one spawned: env 0)
+
+
+def _gf_quat(r: np.ndarray, cls):
+    x, y, z, w = matrix_to_quat(r)
+    return cls(w, x, y, z)
+
+
+def _spawn(prim_path: str, cfg, translation=None, orientation=None, **kwargs):
+    import isaaclab.sim as sim_utils
+    from isaaclab.sim.utils import bind_physics_material, bind_visual_material
+    from isaaclab.sim.utils.stage import get_current_stage
+    from pxr import Gf, PhysxSchema, Sdf, UsdGeom, UsdPhysics
+    from yam_arena.station import linear_rgb
+
+    spec = _SPECS[cfg.part_name]
+    stage = get_current_stage()
+    root = UsdGeom.Xform.Define(stage, prim_path)
+    root.AddTranslateOp(precision=UsdGeom.XformOp.PrecisionDouble).Set(Gf.Vec3d(*(translation or (0.0, 0.0, 0.0))))
+    x, y, z, w = orientation if orientation is not None else (0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)
+    root.AddOrientOp(precision=UsdGeom.XformOp.PrecisionDouble).Set(Gf.Quatd(w, x, y, z))
+    material = f"{prim_path}/Looks/physics"
+    mat = sim_utils.RigidBodyMaterialCfg(static_friction=spec.friction, dynamic_friction=spec.friction)
+    mat.func(material, mat)
+    looks: dict = {}
+
+    def body(path, offset, mass, boxes, radius=0.0):
+        xf = UsdGeom.Xform.Define(stage, path)
+        xf.AddTranslateOp(precision=UsdGeom.XformOp.PrecisionDouble).Set(Gf.Vec3d(*offset))
+        prim = xf.GetPrim()
+        UsdPhysics.RigidBodyAPI.Apply(prim)
+        UsdPhysics.MassAPI.Apply(prim).CreateMassAttr(mass)
+        rb = PhysxSchema.PhysxRigidBodyAPI.Apply(prim)
+        rb.CreateMaxDepenetrationVelocityAttr(1.0)
+        rb.CreateSolverPositionIterationCountAttr(32)
+        if spec.ccd:
+            rb.CreateEnableSpeculativeCCDAttr(True)
+        shapes = list(enumerate(boxes)) + ([(-1, ((0, 0, 0), None, spec.color))] if radius > 0 else [])
+        for i, (centre, size, color, *rot) in shapes:
+            if size is None:
+                geom = UsdGeom.Sphere.Define(stage, f"{path}/sphere")
+                geom.CreateRadiusAttr(radius)
+            else:
+                geom = UsdGeom.Cube.Define(stage, f"{path}/box_{i}")
+                geom.CreateSizeAttr(1.0)
+                geom.AddTranslateOp().Set(Gf.Vec3d(*centre))
+                if rot:
+                    geom.AddRotateZOp().Set(float(rot[0]))
+                if len(rot) > 1:  # then pitched about the box's own y axis (degrees)
+                    geom.AddRotateYOp().Set(float(rot[1]))
+                geom.AddScaleOp().Set(Gf.Vec3f(*size))
+            c = geom.GetPrim()
+            UsdPhysics.CollisionAPI.Apply(c)
+            col = PhysxSchema.PhysxCollisionAPI.Apply(c)
+            col.CreateContactOffsetAttr(spec.contact_offset)
+            col.CreateRestOffsetAttr(0.0)
+            if len(color) > 3 and color[3] == 0:  # a collider that is not drawn (a clear wall)
+                UsdGeom.Imageable(c).MakeInvisible()
+            if color not in looks:
+                looks[color] = f"{prim_path}/Looks/c{len(looks)}"
+                vis = sim_utils.PreviewSurfaceCfg(diffuse_color=linear_rgb(color[:3]), roughness=0.5,
+                                                  opacity=color[3] if len(color) > 3 and color[3] > 0 else 1.0)
+                vis.func(looks[color], vis)
+            bind_physics_material(str(c.GetPath()), material, stage=stage)
+            bind_visual_material(str(c.GetPath()), looks[color], stage=stage)
+        return prim
+
+    main = body(f"{prim_path}/body", (0.0, 0.0, 0.0), spec.mass, spec.boxes, spec.radius)
+    h = spec.hinge
+    if h is not None:
+        child_path = f"{prim_path}/{h.name}_body"
+        body(child_path, h.anchor, h.mass, h.boxes)
+        j = UsdPhysics.RevoluteJoint.Define(stage, f"{child_path}/{h.name}")
+        j.CreateAxisAttr("X")
+        j.CreateBody0Rel().SetTargets([main.GetPath()])
+        j.CreateBody1Rel().SetTargets([Sdf.Path(child_path)])
+        j.CreateLocalPos0Attr(Gf.Vec3f(*h.anchor))
+        j.CreateLocalRot0Attr(_gf_quat(rot_z(h.yaw), Gf.Quatf))
+        j.CreateLocalPos1Attr(Gf.Vec3f(0.0, 0.0, 0.0))
+        j.CreateLocalRot1Attr(_gf_quat(rot_z(h.yaw), Gf.Quatf))
+        j.CreateLowerLimitAttr(math.degrees(h.lower))  # USD revolute limits and drive gains are per degree
+        j.CreateUpperLimitAttr(math.degrees(h.upper))
+        drive = UsdPhysics.DriveAPI.Apply(j.GetPrim(), "angular")
+        drive.CreateTypeAttr("force")
+        drive.CreateStiffnessAttr(h.stiffness * math.pi / 180)
+        drive.CreateDampingAttr(h.damping * math.pi / 180)
+        drive.CreateTargetPositionAttr(0.0)
+        UsdPhysics.ArticulationRootAPI.Apply(main)
+        art = PhysxSchema.PhysxArticulationAPI.Apply(main)
+        art.CreateEnabledSelfCollisionsAttr(False)
+        art.CreateSolverPositionIterationCountAttr(32)
+        art.CreateSolverVelocityIterationCountAttr(4)
+    a = spec.attach
+    if a is not None:
+        # D6 for a screw: the joint frame's x axis (PhysX's unlimited twist axis) is the part's z axis. It turns
+        # freely and slides in [0, travel] along it; the other four axes are locked (low > high).
+        if a.travel > 0:
+            j = UsdPhysics.Joint.Define(stage, f"{prim_path}/{spec.name}_attach")
+            for axis, (lo, hi) in {"transY": (1, -1), "transZ": (1, -1), "rotY": (1, -1), "rotZ": (1, -1),
+                                   "transX": (0.0, a.travel)}.items():
+                lim = UsdPhysics.LimitAPI.Apply(j.GetPrim(), axis)
+                lim.CreateLowAttr(lo)
+                lim.CreateHighAttr(hi)
+            lin = UsdPhysics.DriveAPI.Apply(j.GetPrim(), "transX")
+            lin.CreateTypeAttr("force")
+            lin.CreateStiffnessAttr(a.lin_stiffness)
+            lin.CreateDampingAttr(a.lin_damping)
+            lin.CreateMaxForceAttr(a.lin_max_force)
+            lin.CreateTargetPositionAttr(0.0)
+            lin.CreateTargetVelocityAttr(0.0)
+        else:
+            j = UsdPhysics.RevoluteJoint.Define(stage, f"{prim_path}/{spec.name}_attach")
+            j.CreateAxisAttr("Z")
+        _JOINTS.setdefault(spec.name, str(j.GetPath()))

+def _patch_embodiment(module) -> None:

+

+class _Finder(importlib.abc.MetaPathFinder):

+
+    def find_spec(self, fullname, path, target=None):

+

+            exec_module(module)
+            _TARGETS[fullname](module)
+
+        spec.loader.exec_module = _exec
+        return spec

+def install() -> None:

+        if name in sys.modules:
+            patch(sys.modules[name])
+    if not any(isinstance(f, _Finder) for f in sys.meta_path):
+        sys.meta_path.insert(0, _Finder())
+
+

+  axle with two 18 cm wheels. Its drawbar ends in a painted steel block (80 x 80 mm, 77.5 mm tall) with a towing
+  lug on its front face: a 15 mm steel plate projecting 50 mm toward the robot, 40 mm wide, its top flush with the
+  block's top (lug centre 7 cm above the table), with a 19 mm square hole 30 mm out from the block;
+- a 1/2 in screw-pin D shackle without its pin (galvanised steel, 0.25 kg): 12.7 mm bar, two round ears 27 mm across
+  and 12.7 mm thick with 20.6 mm between them, 47.8 mm inside length. The upper ear has a plain 17.5 mm hole; the
+  lower ear takes the pin's quick-lock thread (a steep lead: half a turn locks it) under a 3.5 mm plain lead-in. It stands upright in a
+  pine stand (a 10 mm base with a slot that holds its lower ear and lower bar), threaded ear down, bow toward the
+  robot, left of the block;
+- its screw pin (steel, red, 0.11 kg): a 15.8 mm pin 46 mm long under a 25 mm collar, with a flat eye 26 mm wide and
+  8 mm thick on top. It stands eye up in a hole through a pine block (40 x 40 x 30 mm), right of the block.
+
+The robot must put the shackle on the lug (the lug between its ears), push the pin through the upper ear, the lug
+and into the lower ear, and lock it with one twist: turned 120 degrees clockwise (seen from above) on the thread, the
+pin latches; half a turn seats its collar.
